sources.title: Jan Antosch, Die deutsche Kolonie Kamerun, Deutsches Historisches Museum (2004)
sources.note: Institutional history directly read. Used for 1884 establishment, 1911 territorial enlargement and 1893/1913 telegraph connections. Its compressed January 1916 ending and 1919 mandate wording are replaced with the more precise campaign and mandate sources below.

sources.title: Treaty of Protection with Chiefs of Cameroon Coast (12 July 1884), Black Central Europe edition
sources.note: Academic public-history edition of the treaty, presented by Robbie Aitken, from Knoll and Hiery, The German Colonial Experience (2010), pages 42 to 43. Direct text read, especially clauses 3 and 5. No claim that the displayed English is a photograph of the original.

sources.title: Sandra Schürmann and Stefan Rahner, Hamburgs koloniale Industrie, Stiftung Historische Museen Hamburg
sources.note: Direct institutional research read, sections Harburger Gummi-Kamm and Kakao- und Schokoladenfabriken. Cameroon claims kept separate from examples in Congo, Nigeria and East Africa.

sources.title: Rudolf Duala Manga Bell: Widerstand gegen die Kolonialmacht in Kamerun, Bundesarchiv
sources.note: Direct archive exhibition and document captions read: 1911 segregation plan, November 1912 petition, January 1913 telegram, September 1913 letter, 1914 petition and proceedings. Biographical commentary supports education, March funding decision and August execution. Avoids its anachronistic description of the birthplace as already a German colony.

sources.title: Bamum Scripts and Archives Project and Charles Riley, Towards the Encoding of the Bamum Script in the UCS (8 January 2006)
sources.note: Direct six-page report read. Page 1: invention with scribes, early logographs, surviving 1906 to 1908 family correspondence and agricultural calendar. Pages 2 to 3: reduction in 1910 and recitation pairs. Dates are approximate and do not imply every Bamum inhabitant was literate.

sources.title: Charles Riley, Report on work with the Bamum script in Cameroon (21 September 2006)
sources.note: Direct four-page first-person field report read. Page 1 gives the exact Latin-transcribed title Ŋga nsapŋam and the English description Collection of Bamum Proverbs for the 1987 edition attributed to Ibrahim Njoya. Pages 1 to 2 identify healer Zakari Nkepu and his teaching chart. Modern continuation explicitly distinguished from the colonial period.

sources.title: Unicode Standard, Bamum code chart, U+A6A0 to U+A6FF
sources.note: Official character chart directly read: PDF page 3 explicitly maps A6A0 ꚠ A, A6A1 ꚡ KA, A6A2 ꚢ U, A6A3 ꚣ KU. Public sample is the first four recitation syllables, not an invented meaningful sentence or a manuscript facsimile.

sources.title: George N. Njung, West Africa, 1914-1918 Online (8 October 2014)
sources.note: Direct scholarly article based on British and Cameroonian archives. PDF pages 4 to 6: Cameroon campaign, local military expertise, refugee displacement, Mora resistance until February 1916 and German retreat to Rio Muni. Public claims do not transfer Gold Coast or Nigerian statistics to Cameroon.

sources.title: United Kingdom report on the Cameroons, United Nations document T/1090, historical account paragraphs 60 to 62
sources.note: Official report indexed text directly exposed paragraphs 60 to 62 in search; direct PDF fetch returned an error. Paragraph 60: provisional partition effective 18 April 1916 and boundary adjustments in 1920 following the 10 July 1919 declaration. Paragraph 61: Versailles renunciation and mandate instrument of 20 July 1922. Colonial administrative testimony is used for formal dates, not as a neutral account of popular consent.

proposedOverrides.name: Kamerun
proposedOverrides.summary: A German colonial territory whose conquest and wartime partition disrupted diverse African societies.

batchIdentityNotes.decision: Standalone colonial narrative, not an alias of modern Cameroon. The expanded 1914 outline is compatible with the 1911 Neukamerun additions. The imported display interval is explicitly distinguished from German colonial control, 1884 to 1916, and the 1922 mandates. Period boundaries do not overlap except shared transition endpoints.
batchIdentityNotes.writing: Exact scholarly Latin transcription of a title, with the source’s English collection description. No reconstructed Bamum glyphs and no claim that a modern publication is a surviving colonial manuscript.
